page.layout: Running head at top left: "LIB. II. Scutum Regium." Page number at top right: 77. One text column, with a single marginal note on the right, beside the text at "quòd". No catchword, signature or footnote. Only the left printed page is visible; the scan edge at the far left belongs to the neighbouring page.

main_text.p: Traiani exemplum, non tantùm admonebat; sed propemodùm compellebat. Siquidem quæ ab ipso facta essent sancta vtique & pia, atque omni ex parte iustissima censerentur: neque iam de illis legitima exercebantur iudicia, velut in caufis etiam criminosorum fieri consueuit, sed clamore vulgi fidelcs delati, tanquam de crimine conuicti neci dabantur, vt apparet ex literis Sereniy Graniani Proconsulis, ad Adrianum Imperatorem, & Rescriptis Adriani ad Minutium Fundanum. Quanta tamen eorum, etiam his temporibns copia & magnanimitas fuerit, vel exinde constat, quòd {*}Arrius Antoninus, dum Prouinciam administraret in Asia, in ciuitate quæ Christianam Religionem fuerat amplexata; omnes, qui in ea erant fideles, pro tribunali sedentem adiere, palàm se Christianos esse profitentes, eaque de causa omnes se libenter mortem oppetituros. Cum is rei magnitudine & nouitate perterritus, paucis ex illis damnatis, in reliquos vt præcipitia atque suspendia (si mori optarent) sibi sponte deligerent, exclamauit:Tertul. ad Scapulam vlt.

page.notes: Printing errors left as printed: "fidelcs" (for fideles), "temporibns" (for temporibus), "sancta" read as sancta. "Sereniy" is doubtful: the italic word after "literis" may be "Serenissimi" or a similar form, so the reading is uncertain. The word "Cum" after "oppetituros." is read as printed, with an accent that may be a grave mark. The reference mark "*" in the text is matched to the marginal note "Tertul. ad Scapulam vlt.".
